full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal, are that the petitioner herein as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.3801 of 2008 before the Assistant Judge, Fourth Court, Gazipur, for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. The plaintiff stated, inter alia, that the suit property belonged to Bhagaban Chandra Chanda, whose name was recorded in C.S. Khatian No.157. Bhagaban Chandra Chanda died leaving behind 5 sons, namely Bhupendra Chandra Chanda, Nripendra Chandra Chanda, Pabitra Chandra Chanda, Amulya Chandra Chanda and Shailendra alias Susil Chandra Chanda and their names have been recorded in the S.A. Khatian No.246 in the plot No.253 and they transferred 2.99 acres of land including the suit land to Sudhir Chandra Chanda, father of the plaintiff through kabala No.1419 dated 19.03.1969 and delivered possession. The plaintiff submitted the certified copy of the kabala No.1419 dated 19.03.1969 as the original has been destroyed by fire. Sudhir Chandra Chanda died leaving the plaintiff as the only son, who having got the suit land by inheritance being in peaceful possession of the same by paying the rents duly and R.S. Khatian No. 203 was wrongly recorded in the name of the defendants. Deed No.344 dated 02.02.1962 and deed No.977 dated 04.03.1963 had been fraudulently created by the defendants. The plaintiff went to the local Tashil Office on 25.09.2005 and came to know that R.S. Khatian No.203 has been recorded in the name of the defendants. Hence, the plaintiff filed the suit. After institution of the suit on 20.05.2006 the defendants dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land and built a small but thereon. Therefore, the plaintiff prayed for decree for declaration of title as well as recovery of khan possession. 

 3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint. They contended, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form; that the suit is barred by limitation, barred by waiver, estoppel and acquiescence. The defendant, and upon his death, his heirs claimed that the heirs of the original tenant Bhagaban Chandra Chanda transferred the suit land to Naresh Chandra Chanda, son of late Saraf Chandra Chanda through kabala No.344 dated 02.02.1962 and delivered possession. Dilip Kumar Chanda inherited the suit land from Naresh Chandra Chanda and transferred to the predecessor of defendants through kabala No.977 dated 04.03.1963. R.S. Khatian No.203 has been recorded in the name of defendant No.1. The defendants claimed that 5 sons of Bhagaban Chandra Chanda left for India before R.S. record and the kabala No.1419 dated 10.03.1969 is a forged deed. The plaintiff has no right, title and interest in the suit land. The defendants claimed that the plaintiff filed this test suit which is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 13. The appellate Court observed that there was no evidence that the plaintiff was in possession of the suit land before 20.5.2006. It was noted that P.W. 2(the borgadar of the plaintiff) mentioned that the plaintiff was dispossessed by the defendant on 20.5.2006, but he did not state that he was in possession of the suit land on behalf of the plaintiff, and P.W. 3 could not give the date of the dispossession. The appellate Court concluded that the plaintiff was not able to prove the story of dispossession by sufficient evidence. On the other hand, R.S. survey was held regarding the suit land, and on the basis of the deed dated 04.03.1963 R.S. Khatian No. 203 was prepared in the name of Kazi Idris Ali and, therefore, it was accepted that Kazi Idris Ali was in possession of the suit land that is why the R.S. record was prepared in his name. This was also supported by the evidence of D.W. 1, 3 and 4.
